title: Lean Muscle Mass Isn’t a Cure-All for Metabolic Health - Nautilus
author: Jake Currie
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementHealthLean Muscle Mass Isn’t a Cure-All for Metabolic HealthA new study is complicating the pictureJCBy Jake Currie6:00 PM CST on November 10, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleYou’ve probably heard it your entire adult life—building lean muscle mass is one of the best things you can do for your health. After all, in addition to boosting physical strength and burning calories, lean muscle mass also pulls glucose from the blood and helps protect against diabetes. But now a new study published in The Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism is challenging that conventional wisdom.A team of nutritional and chronic disease researchers from Louisiana State University analyzed health data from close to 60,000 adults (between the ages of 37 and 73) enrolled in the U.K. Biobank study. They focused on those who had undergone MRI and low-level X-ray scans capable of determining their fat-free mass, a commonly used proxy for lean muscle mass. Read more: “People With This Neanderthal Hormone Receptor Have More Muscle Mass”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
